item.text:
**4B.10 Verdict**
- **Weaker overall.** Pakistan’s democratic baseline was already damaged before Sharif returned, and 2024 mostly extended or deepened the same pattern: coercive digital controls, media pressure, protest repression, and weaker judicial independence. The main positives were procedural continuity, not substantive freedom-building.

**Evidence**
- **Pakistan: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/pakistan/freedom-world/2024)  
  Pakistan stayed **Partly Free**, but Freedom House’s score fell from **37 to 35** versus the prior year. The overview says the military intimidates the media and authorities impose selective civil-liberties restrictions, so the inherited baseline was already weakening.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.4`

- **Pakistan: New Government Should Protect Rights** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-11 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/11/pakistan-new-government-should-protect-rights)  
  HRW’s letter shows what a stronger outcome would have required: reversing abusive laws and strengthening democratic institutions. This is counterfactual rather than proof of progress, but it marks how far Sharif still had to go.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`

- **Pakistan’s largest parties strike deal on coalition government** | Reuters | 2024-02-21 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government/1973213/)  
  PML-N and PPP formally agreed to govern together after the hung election, which is the main positive sign that office transfer still ran through coalition bargaining and constitutional procedure.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.8`, `4B.1`

- **Pakistan’s newly elected assembly meets amid pro-Imran Khan protests** | Reuters | 2024-02-29 | [URL](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Pakistan%27s%2Bnewly%2Belected%2Bassembly%2Bmeets%2Bamid%2Bpro-Imran%2BKhan%2Bprotests/22856039.html)  
  The assembly met on time, so the constitutional machinery still functioned, but the environment was already deeply disputed and destabilized.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.8`

- **Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif takes oath as prime minister** | Reuters | 2024-03-04 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/pakistans-shehbaz-sharif-takes-oath-as-prime-minister-3322834)  
  Sharif returned through the normal parliamentary route after the election and caretaker period. That supports continuity, but it is only procedural resilience, not evidence of a freer political order.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.8`

- **Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights** | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/)  
  The election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown created a coercive information environment around Sharif’s ascent and chilled expression and assembly. Even though it was caretaker-era, Sharif inherited the fallout and did not reverse it.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.8`

- **Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent)  
  HRW says the government had already clamped down on media, the opposition, and NGOs, and the 2024 environment continued that trajectory rather than correcting it. This is strong evidence that democratic resilience started weak and stayed weak.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`

- **Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs** | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | [URL](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps)  
  The 26th Amendment altered senior-judge appointments in ways critics said weakened judicial independence, with allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. That points to a weaker accountability environment by year-end.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.8`

- **Pakistan: Controversial Punjab Defamation Act Signed into Law** | Library of Congress | 2024-06-25 / 2024-06-26 | [URL](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-06-25/pakistan-controversial-punjab-defamation-act-signed-into-law)  
  Punjab’s defamation law created tribunal and platform-suspension powers that critics said could be weaponized against critics and media. That strengthens political control, not democratic resilience.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`

- **A dangerous digital crackdown** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown)  
  HRW says the government was expanding internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls while keeping X blocked. By late 2024, the digital environment was more controlled, not more open.  
  IDs: `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9`

**Search gap**
- I found no strong 2024 evidence that Sharif materially reversed the inherited crackdown or built durable new protections for media, protest, or judicial independence.
- The best positive evidence is procedural: coalition bargaining, parliamentary election, and normal oath-taking. That keeps the answer from being “much weaker,” but it is not enough to offset the substantive backsliding.
